title: iPhone 12 & 13: The Last Great iPhones With Headphone Jacks
meta_description: iPhone 14+ removed the headphone jack. iPhone 12 & 13 refurbished give you modern performance plus the features Apple took away. Music lovers, this one's for you.
content:
iPhone 12 & 13: The Last Great iPhones With Headphone Jacks

Apple removed the headphone jack from iPhone 14 and newer models. Yeah, that feature you actually use.

So you're stuck choosing between modern performance and keeping your wired headphones. Or buying dongles that disappear. Or accepting that your $200 studio monitors are now paperweights.

What if you didn't have to choose?

The Sweet Spot Nobody Talks About

iPhone 12 and iPhone 13 are the last models with built-in headphone jacks. They run iOS 17 perfectly, have the same camera quality as newer models, and handle every app you throw at them.

But here's what makes them perfect right now: refurbished prices.

A new iPhone 15 costs $799 and forces you to use wireless everything. A refurbished iPhone 13 costs $349 and lets you plug in whatever you want. Same performance, half the price, plus the feature Apple took away.

iPhone 13 Refurbished -- Excellent from $349

All the modern iPhone features plus the headphone jack Apple removed. Perfect for music lovers who refuse to compromise.

Check availability

Why Audio People Choose These Models

Studio headphones. IEMs. That vintage pair you've had for years. They all work instantly without adapters or battery anxiety.

You can charge and listen simultaneously -- try that with Lightning dongles that break every six months. The audio quality is identical to newer models because Apple didn't change the DAC, just removed the port.

Plus you get modern features newer phone users take for granted: MagSafe charging, 5G, computational photography, Face ID that works with masks. Everything current except the arbitrary feature removal.

iPhone 12 Refurbished -- Excellent from $289

Budget option that still gives you the headphone jack plus 5G, Face ID, and years of iOS updates ahead.

Check availability

The Battery Reality Check

Our iPhone 13 inventory averages 89% battery health. That's better than most one-year-old phones and will easily last you two more years of normal use.

iPhone 12 units average 86% battery health -- still excellent and priced accordingly. When you're saving $450 vs new, you can afford a battery replacement in year three if needed.

Every device ships with exact battery percentage disclosed upfront. No surprises, no degraded batteries sold as "excellent." You know exactly what you're getting.

FAQ

Do iPhone 12 and 13 still get iOS updates?

Yes, both run iOS 17 perfectly and will receive updates for at least 3-4 more years. Apple typically supports iPhones for 6-7 years from launch, so you're covered through 2028-2029.

What's the audio quality difference vs newer iPhones?

Zero difference. Apple didn't change the internal audio processing, just removed the physical port. Same DAC, same sound quality, but you can actually use your existing headphones.

Will my wired headphones work with these models?

Any headphones with standard 3.5mm plugs work directly. No dongles, no adapters, no charging required. Plug in and listen like phones used to work.

Sometimes the best upgrade is getting the features back that newer models took away. Your headphones work, your wallet stays happy, and you get modern performance without the compromises.
